question: Which document, slice, schema, format, diagnostic and application contracts should own external document imports, and which editing-runtime requirements can disappear?
trigger: The accepted conversion vocabulary and hidden-envelope hard cut required reusable doctrine repair and exact generated-skill proof before final closure.
requirements: Retain the settled HTML, Markdown, DOCX, authored JSON, schema-admission, diagnostic, and pure/editor ownership decisions.
Teach operation-law naming and the independent-job gate for hidden native payloads at the reusable owners.
Regenerate agent mirrors, bump Plate Next doctrine, and preserve package adoption as a separate outcome.
Do not add a new converter, codec, persistence channel, or product implementation in this design pass.
evidenceReuse: Reused the preceding import and export vocabulary reviews and their fixed-source comparison. Rechecked the repaired Best API source, Plate vision, generated Codex and Claude mirrors, Plate Next doctrine version, current export decision, and package-attestation boundary. No product source or call shape changed during this closure.
summary: Reaffirm the import/conversion target after doctrine repair. HTML and Markdown use parse/serialize with complete-document defaults and explicit slice/inline suffixes; editor delegates reuse installed configuration and standalone functions compile supplied declarations. DOCX remains importDocx/exportDocx. Encode/decode stays with typed pairs. Hidden authored HTML/Markdown payloads remain deleted in favor of canonical authored JSON and DOCX review. Best API and Plate vision now teach the same law, generated mirrors are exact, and Plate Next v238 records it without claiming package adoption.

reconciliation.reason: The call shape, schema and diagnostics laws, pure/editor ownership, DOCX boundary, and envelope deletion remain unchanged.

reconciliation.question: Which document, slice, schema, format, diagnostic and application contracts should own external document imports, and which editing-runtime requirements can disappear?
reconciliation.reason: The design remains valid, but final closure must bind repaired reusable doctrine, generated mirror parity, and Plate Next v238 through a fresh plan outcome.

alternatives: Leave naming and hidden-state taste only in the feature plan: Stop; later Best API reviews could repeat the rejected codec and envelope shapes.
Copy the full product decision into every worker skill: Stop; Best API and Plate vision are the durable owners and downstream skills already route reusable call-shape decisions there.
Repair the canonical rules, regenerate mirrors, and preserve adoption limits: Pursue; this closes teaching without pretending the product has migrated.
proofLimits: Doctrine and design proof only. No product API, package, caller, docs, tests, browser route, packed consumer, DOCX artifact, native viewer, or runtime behavior was changed or rerun. Current product code still exposes the old names and authored HTML/Markdown envelopes. Plate Next v238 changes doctrine only; packages retain their last proven applied versions.
